title: Python Tutorial
description: Master Python step-by-step, from installation to advanced OOP concepts. Includes interactive code challenges and practical examples for each topic.

content.content: Python can be installed from the official Python website: https://www.python.org/downloads/

content: Download the installer for your OS
Run the installer and check 'Add Python to PATH'
Verify installation by running `python --version` in your terminal

content.content: Python syntax can be executed directly in the command line or from a file.

questions.question: Write a Python program to print 'Hello, Python!'

content.content: Comments are used to explain code. They start with a # symbol.

questions.question: Write a comment saying 'My first program' and print Hello

content.content: Variables are containers for storing data values.

questions.question: Create a variable age with value 25 and print it

content.content: Python has various data types such as int, float, str, bool, list, tuple, set, and dict.

x = 5         # int
y = 3.14      # float
z = "Hello"   # str

questions.question: Create variables of int, float, and string type and print each

content.content: Python supports integers, floating-point numbers, and complex numbers.

x = 1     # int
y = 2.8   # float
z = 1j    # complex

questions.question: Assign a complex number 3+5j to a variable and print it

content.content: Casting is used to convert variables from one type to another.

x = int(1.5)
y = float(2)
z = str(3)

questions.question: Convert float 5.99 to int and print it

content.content: Strings in Python are surrounded by either single or double quotes.

questions.question: Store 'Python' in a variable and print the first 3 letters

content.content: Booleans represent True or False values.

questions.question: Write an expression that returns True if 7 is greater than 3

content.content: Operators are used to perform operations on variables and values.

x = 5
y = 3
print(x + y)
print(x - y)
print(x * y)
print(x / y)
Lists are used to store multiple items in a single variable.

questions.question: Create a list of 3 numbers and print the second number

content.content: Tuples are ordered and unchangeable collections.

questions.question: Create a tuple of 3 fruits and print the last one

content.content: Sets are unordered and do not allow duplicate values.

questions.question: Create a set with values 1, 2, 3 and print it

content.content: Dictionaries are used to store data values in key:value pairs.

questions.question: Create a dictionary with name and age, print name

content.content: Python supports if, elif, and else conditions.

a = 33
b = 200
if b > a:
    print("b is greater than a")

questions.question: Write an if statement that prints 'Yes' if 5 is less than 10

content.content: Match is used for pattern matching, similar to switch in other languages.

x = 2
match x:
    case 1:
        print("One")
    case 2:
        print("Two")

questions.question: Write a match statement that prints 'Three' if variable is 3
